players.product: diesel standby gensets (95 L / QSK95) and QSK60 / HSK78 natural gas gensets for data centers; 130 L natural gas prime-power genset in development

quarterly_data.signal: First quarter sales were $8.4 billion, up 3%, 'driven primarily by higher demand in power generation markets, particularly from data centers', partly offset by weaker North America heavy and medium duty truck demand; EBITDA excluding the $199 million net charge on the low-pressure fuel cell sale was $1.5 billion or 17.7%.
quarterly_data.figure: sales $8.4 billion (+3%); EBITDA ex-charge $1.5 billion or 17.7%

quarterly_data.signal: Power Systems segment revenues were $2 billion, an increase of 19%, with record EBITDA rising from 23.6% to 29.5% of sales on volumes, positive pricing, net tariff recovery, higher joint venture income and one-time cost recoveries; North America power generation revenues increased 23%, 'driven primarily by continued strong data center demand'.
quarterly_data.figure: Power Systems revenue $2 billion (+19%); EBITDA 23.6% to 29.5%; North America power generation +23%

quarterly_data.signal: China: sales of power generation equipment increased 84% in the quarter 'due to accelerating data center demand'; China revenues including joint ventures were $2.1 billion (+19%), and the 2026 China revenue outlook was raised to +10% from a prior down 1%, driven by stronger data center demand. Management: 'the big change in China has been this dramatic increase in power generation to support data centers'.
quarterly_data.figure: China power generation equipment sales +84%; China revenue $2.1 billion (+19%); 2026 China revenue outlook +10% (prior down 1%)

quarterly_data.signal: Raised 2026 outlook: global power generation revenues now +15%-25% (prior 10%-20%), reflecting 'accelerating data center demand supported by capacity additions we brought on in North America at the end of 2025' plus stronger international growth (China, Asia Pacific) and increased demand for lower output gen sets 'amid ongoing capacity constraints'; total company revenue +8%-11% (prior 3%-8%), EBITDA 17.75%-18.5%.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 power generation revenue +15%-25% (prior 10%-20%); total revenue +8%-11% (prior 3%-8%); EBITDA 17.75%-18.5%

quarterly_data.signal: Power Systems 2026 guidance raised to revenue growth of 14%-19% (prior 12%-17%) on stronger demand, especially international, with EBITDA margins of approximately 25%-26% (prior 23%-24%); remaining-year margins expected strong but a little below Q1 given uneven tariff costs/recoveries and Q1 one-time cost recoveries.

Distribution segment revenues rose 7% to $3.1 billion with EBITDA 14.2% (vs 12.9%), driven by higher power generation demand; full-year 2026 Distribution revenue guidance raised to +9%-14% (prior 5%-10%) 'due to stronger demand for power generation equipment, mainly'.

Capacity: IR (Nick Arens) said Cummins 'doubled the capacity of the 95-liter, finished that investment last year', continues to see strong demand with 'multi-year discussions with our customers around their needs', and is evaluating additional capacity investments across plants and supply chain to be detailed at the May 21 Analyst Day. (An analyst cited industry 95-liter lead times into the back half of 2028; management did not confirm a date.)

2026 capital investments expected in the range of $1.35 billion-$1.45 billion 'as we continue to make critical investments to support future growth'; CFO said Power Systems is 'investing in raising capacities to meet even stronger demand'.
